Let's talk math for increasing Trump's odds for the final election. His odds of winning the nomination are 78% (+-) a bit because that market has less liquidity. His odds all out are 25%. Seperating the two processes that's 78% of nomination and 32% for the nation if nominated. We will call the nomination Pn at .78, Pgi at 32% for general isolated, and Pf at 25% for the final probability.

Pf = Pn * Pgi

Boringly simple partial derivitive just to make my point.

∂Pf = ∂Pn * ∂Pgi

You get much more improvement on his final stats by bumping up his odds in the general. By 2.5x Not only that but you can never get to 100% in either. It is much easier to add 5% to Pgi and you will get 2.5x more out of it. If you compare the others in the general you get similar results.
